text:
Most of the studies on weight regain after stopping these drugs involved taking the patient to top the maximum level of the drug for at least 6 to 12 months and then cutting them off cold turkey.
However a few studies have involved titrating the dose down slowly over time, and also continuing dietitian and exercise support. In those cases, the majority of patients maintain their weight loss. If they continued the drug, they did so at a very low dose. 
Also, we are learning that taking the maximum dose is not always necessary. Good obesity doctors are recommending that patients take no higher of a dose than is necessary to lose weight at a reasonable rate.
I lost 50 lb using tirzepatide over the course of a year, which is less than a pound a week. I ate plenty of protein and did lots of weight-bearing exercise.
Less than 10% of my weight loss was lean body mass, the rest was fat.
I never went above 2/3 of the maximum dose and that only for a few months. Mostly I was on half the maximum dose. 
Now that I'm at goal weight, I've been titrating down and have maintained for about 6 weeks. 
The medical community is learning more about these drugs as time goes on, but I think the approach that my doctor and I have used will turn out to be more effective long-term. He says that the vast majority of his patients are on the minimum dose, a microdose, or have managed to titrate completely off of the drugs.

text: I tried Ozempic for a little over a year.  I started at the .25 mg dose and went up to the .5 mg dose.  I had nausea with vomiting the first few days after my injection each week.  Even though I was careful about what I ate and not eating too late in the day, I would get nausea in the morning - often on an empty stomach - and it made getting ready for work challenging.  I took a 4 mg Zofran pill to help with the nausea on those days.  My care provider suggested I go back to the .25 mg dose of Ozempic to see if the lower dose would help, as I was still experiencing nausea after nine months of being on Ozempic.  My nausea never went away, so I eventually stopped taking Ozempic.  However, my blood glucose levels rose and I regained the 20 lbs. I had lost while on Ozempic, which was disappointing.  Now, I just recently switched to a different diabetes drug.  Hopefully the new drug works for me.  I think Ozempic was great for making me feel full faster and for the weight I lost.  I still think Ozempic is well worth using - if it works for you and you can handle the side effects.  My husband also takes Ozempic at the higher 1 mg dose and he does not have any of the negative side effects.  It leads me to believe that it just depends on the individual.
